tools.name: list_monitors
tools.description: Paginated monitors in the project. Optional status filter (up/down/paused/ssl_expiring).

tools.name: get_monitor
tools.description: Fetch a single monitor by its UUID.

tools.name: create_monitor
tools.description: Create a new monitor. Requires name+url; add "port" for port checks, "dns_*" for DNS checks.

tools.name: update_monitor
tools.description: Patch a monitor. Pass only fields you want to change; others are preserved.

tools.name: pause_monitor
tools.description: Pause a monitor — no checks run and no alerts fire. Same as update_monitor with paused=true.

tools.name: resume_monitor
tools.description: Resume a paused monitor. Same as update_monitor with paused=false.

tools.name: search_monitors_by_name
tools.description: Case-insensitive substring search across monitor names and URLs.

tools.name: get_status_summary
tools.description: Up/down/paused counts plus a list of currently down monitors with the timestamp they went down.

tools.name: list_outages
tools.description: Paginated list of outages in the project. Filter by status, type, or search term.

tools.name: get_outage
tools.description: Fetch a single outage by UUID, including acknowledgements, description, and root cause.

tools.name: get_outage_timeline
tools.description: Full activity timeline for an outage: detection, cross-region verification, alert dispatches, acknowledgement, resolution.

tools.name: get_monitor_outages
tools.description: Paginated list of outages scoped to one monitor. Convenience wrapper around list_outages.

tools.name: create_outage
tools.description: Declare an incident by hand, for a problem no monitor detects. It appears under Incident Management in the dashboard and, with an escalation policy, pages its on-call responders. Internal: nothing is published on a status page (create_status_page_incident does that).

tools.name: acknowledge_outage
tools.description: Mark an ongoing outage as being handled: repeat alerts stop. Escalation steps still fire on schedule; resolve it or fix the cause to stop them.

tools.name: escalate_outage
tools.description: Page the next step of the outage's escalation policy now instead of waiting for it. Each call moves one step further.

tools.name: resolve_outage
tools.description: Resolve an incident declared by hand or a server incident, and send the recovery to the channels it paged. An outage detected on a monitor resolves itself when its checks pass again.

tools.name: list_recent_alerts
tools.description: Alert notifications (up/down transitions) over a date range. Defaults to last 30 days.

tools.name: get_monitor_uptime
tools.description: Uptime percentage over a date window, aggregated and optionally per day/hour/week/month.

tools.name: get_monitor_response_time
tools.description: Response time latency trend over a date window. Returns a per-monitor breakdown — pass all monitors at once in monitor_uuids rather than calling this once per monitor.

tools.name: get_monitor_mttr
tools.description: Mean time to resolve (MTTR) per monitor over a date window, in seconds. Already per-monitor — pass all monitors at once in monitor_uuids rather than calling this once per monitor.

tools.name: get_monitor_mtta
tools.description: Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) per monitor over a date window, in seconds. Already per-monitor — pass all monitors at once in monitor_uuids rather than calling this once per monitor.

tools.name: get_monitor_anomalies
tools.description: Anomaly-detection output for a single monitor (flapping, latency spikes, etc.).

tools.name: get_monitor_http_logs
tools.description: Recent HTTP probe logs for a monitor, paginated. Useful to diagnose recent check failures.

tools.name: list_on_call_schedules
tools.description: All on-call schedules in the project. Each entry typically includes rotation config and current on-call.

tools.name: get_on_call_schedule
tools.description: One schedule by UUID with full rotation detail and the linked escalation policies.

tools.name: list_escalation_policies
tools.description: All escalation policies in the project. Use to find which monitors route alerts where.

tools.name: get_escalation_policy
tools.description: One policy by UUID. Reveals step sequence, linked schedules, and contact channels.

tools.name: list_team_members
tools.description: Users on the project, with names and emails. Use to resolve user IDs from schedules/policies.

tools.name: get_on_call_now
tools.description: Who is on call, per on-call schedule, right now or at the moment given in `at` (e.g. next Saturday 10:00), computed by the engine that pages people: names, emails and the rotation of each person, and the escalation policies each schedule pages for. Use it for any "who is on call" question instead of

tools.name: list_integrations
tools.description: All notification integrations in the project (Slack, Telegram, Discord, PagerDuty, OpsGenie, Teams, webhook, etc.).

tools.name: get_integration
tools.description: One integration by UUID, with its channel-specific config (channel name, webhook URL, routing, etc.).

tools.name: list_status_pages
tools.description: Status pages in the project, 20 per page: UUID, name, public URL, password protection.

tools.name: get_status_page
tools.description: One status page with its settings (languages, subscriptions, access) and the services it shows, section by section, with their UUIDs and type (monitor, healthcheck, server or component).

tools.name: create_status_page
tools.description: Create a status page on a hyperping.app subdomain, with sections of monitors, healthchecks, components and servers. It is public as soon as it exists: confirm the name, address and services with the user first. Password protection, SSO, a custom domain and a logo are set in the dashboard.

tools.name: update_status_page
tools.description: Change a status page's name, description, website, look or subscription button. Only the fields passed change. The page is public: confirm the change with the user first.

tools.name: add_status_page_services
tools.description: Show monitors, healthchecks, components or servers on a status page, in the section you name (created at the end if the page has none by that name) or the first one. Services already on the page stay where they are. A healthcheck shows its uptime bar (show_uptime) but never response times.

tools.name: remove_status_page_services
tools.description: Take monitors, healthchecks, components or servers off a status page, wherever they appear, groups included. Their settings on the page (display name, description) are lost.

tools.name: list_status_page_incidents
tools.description: Incidents published on status pages, newest first, each with its current stage and latest update. For downtime detected on monitors, use list_outages.

tools.name: get_status_page_incident
tools.description: One status page incident with every update (newest first, with their UUIDs), its status pages and affected components.

tools.name: create_status_page_incident
tools.description: Publish an incident on status pages, with its first update. Public, and emailed to subscribers unless notify_subscribers is false: confirm the wording with the user first. To record an incident internally and page on-call instead, use create_outage.

tools.name: add_status_page_incident_update
tools.description: Post an update on a status page incident (investigating, identified, update, monitoring, resolved). Public, and sent to subscribers unless notify_subscribers is false.

tools.name: resolve_status_page_incident
tools.description: Close a status page incident with a final "resolved" update. Same as add_status_page_incident_update with status "resolved"; refuses an incident that is already resolved.

tools.name: update_status_page_incident
tools.description: Change a status page incident's title, type, status pages or affected services. The pages show the change right away; subscribers are not notified. To tell them something, post an update.

tools.name: edit_status_page_incident_update
tools.description: Correct the text or stage of an update already posted, e.g. a typo. The page shows the correction; subscribers are not notified again and its date is kept.

tools.name: list_maintenance_windows
tools.description: Maintenance windows, 20 per page, with their monitors, status pages, updates and status (upcoming, inprogress, completed).

tools.name: get_maintenance_window
tools.description: One maintenance window with its updates and the state of its subscriber notification.

tools.name: create_maintenance_window
tools.description: Schedule a maintenance window: checks and alerts stop for its monitors during the window, and the status pages you pass announce it. Public once it has status pages: confirm with the user first.

tools.name: update_maintenance_window
tools.description: Reschedule a maintenance window, rename it, change its monitors or status pages, or post a public update on it. The pages show the change; subscribers are not notified.

tools.name: complete_maintenance_window
tools.description: End a maintenance window in progress now: checks and alerts resume on its monitors and the status pages show it as completed.

tools.name: cancel_maintenance_window
tools.description: Cancel a maintenance window that has not started: it is deleted and leaves the status pages. Subscribers already told about it are not told it is cancelled. To end one in progress, use complete_maintenance_window.

tools.name: search_logs
tools.description: Search the project's logs, newest first. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_monitors_by_name, list_recent_alerts, list_team_members, get_on_call_now, list_integrations, get_integration, list_status_pages, get_maintenance_window, get_outage_logs, get_recent_changes, list_audit_log, get_outage_alerts · Private data: get_escalation_policy, list_status_pages, create_status_page, create_status_page_incident, get_outage_checks, list_audit_log · Public sink: resolve_outage, list_integrations, get_integration, create_status_page_incident, add_status_page_incident_update, update_status_page_incident, update_maintenance_window, summarize_log_errors, find_correlated_outages, list_audit_log, get_outage_alerts · Destructive: pause_monitor, remove_status_page_services, list_log_dashboards, run_log_chart, run_check_now, get_healthcheck, get_browser_run.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_monitors_by_name, list_recent_alerts, list_team_members, get_on_call_now, list_integrations, get_integration, list_status_pages, get_maintenance_window, get_outage_logs, get_recent_changes, list_audit_log, get_outage_alerts · Private data: get_escalation_policy, list_status_pages, create_status_page, create_status_page_incident, get_outage_checks, list_audit_log · Public sink: resolve_outage, list_integrations, get_integration, create_status_page_incident, add_status_page_incident_update, update_status_page_incident, update_maintenance_window, summarize_log_errors, find_correlated_outages, list_audit_log, get_outage_alerts · Destructive: pause_monitor, remove_status_page_services, list_log_dashboards, run_log_chart, run_check_now, get_healthcheck, get_browser_run

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
